patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient reports a 2-month history of fatigue and several episodes of lower abdominal pain. She expresses a strong belief that she has cancer and desires a diagnostic laparoscopy. The patient has been off work for 2 weeks on sick leave due to stress at work and wishes to return. She was diagnosed with peptic ulcer disease 6 months ago.

Secondary_Symptoms: Desire for diagnostic laparoscopy due to cancer concern

patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Works as a nurse. No mention of smoking, alcohol use, or recreational drug use.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Reports tiredness and depressed mood. No mention of changes in bowel or urinary habits.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and manage a patient presenting with fatigue, stress, and concern for cancer.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “I’m a 26-year-old nurse, and for about two months I’ve been feeling very fatigued and I’ve had a few episodes of lower abdominal pain. I’m also feeling quite stressed at work, and I’ve been worried about cancer and would like to discuss whether diagnostic laparoscopy is appropriate.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any yellowing of my skin or my eyes. I mostly just feel very tired and have had those episodes of lower abdominal pain.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel stiffness in your joints or muscles when you wake up in the morning? If yes, does it usually improve after you start moving around?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I don’t have noticeable joint or muscle stiffness when I wake up, and I don’t feel like it improves after I start moving.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling confused lately—like you’re having trouble thinking clearly, staying oriented, or understanding what’s going on?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t been confused or had trouble thinking clearly or staying oriented. I just feel very tired and worried, and it’s making it hard to focus at times.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been having night sweats—waking up with your clothes or bedding noticeably damp—recently? (Yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had night sweats or woken up with my clothes or bedding damp.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed a lump or swelling in your thigh that feels like it’s within the muscle (not just on the skin)?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any lump or swelling in my thigh—nothing that feels like it’s within the muscle. I’ve mainly just been dealing with fatigue and intermittent lower abdominal pain, along with the stress and worry about what it could be.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any skin lesions, sores, or unusual bumps along the veins on your arm (for example, in a line or track where the veins are)?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any unusual skin lesions, sores, or bumps along the veins on my arms. I haven’t seen anything that looks like a line or track—just the fatigue and those intermittent episodes of lower abdominal pain.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever worked in a job where you might breathe in metal dust or metal fumes—for example welding, grinding, cutting, machining, construction/renovation, or working with batteries or metal plating? (Yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: “No—at work I’m a nurse, and I haven’t been exposed to metal dust or metal fumes like welding, grinding, or machining. I’ve mostly just been dealing with fatigue, intermittent lower abdominal pain, and the stress from work.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any bony enlargement or swelling around your joints (for example, fingers, knuckles, knees, or hips), such as bumps that seem to be part of the bone rather than just soft swelling?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any bony enlargement or swelling around my joints—no bumps on my fingers, knuckles, knees, or hips. I’m mainly still dealing with fatigue and those intermittent lower abdominal pain episodes.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you currently have pain in your thigh (either left or right)?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I don’t have pain in my thigh right now—my main issues are the fatigue and the intermittent lower abdominal pain. I’m not noticing any leg pain.”

turns.doctor_question: I’m sorry you’re dealing with this—can I ask: **do you experience pain or discomfort during sex (either at the entrance or deeper inside)?**
turns.patient_answer: “I haven’t noticed any pain or discomfort during sex—no pain at the entrance or deeper inside. My main symptoms are the fatigue and intermittent lower abdominal pain, along with a lot of stress and worry about cancer.”
